text:
Relative position and elapsed time provide complementary signals: interaction distance captures sequence locality; timestamp gaps distinguish rapid bursts from widely separated actions. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) combines position and pairwise time-interval embeddings inside attention. [MEANTIME](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08273) is especially relevant to a BERT4Rec extension: multiple temporal embeddings and attention heads capture different behavioral patterns within one jointly trained network. More recent [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings with temporal-proximity contrastive learning. These papers motivate temporal modeling, but do not establish gains under the pinned Amazon evaluation.

A lightweight experiment inferred from these approaches: retain the bidirectional BERT4Rec backbone and add per-head attention biases for bucketed signed positional distance and log-bucketed observed timestamp differences. Let heads learn different temporal sensitivities rather than forcing every head toward recent events; this could represent immediate intent alongside persistent interests. Compute history recency relative to the last observed event. For the appended prediction mask, use a learned unknown-time relation, or explicitly treat last-event-relative recency as a feature; never supply the held-out event timestamp. Preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference, following [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). Compare position-only, time-only and combined biases using macro validation HR@10. Improved validation would support predictive utility; weak permutation effects alone cannot establish that temporal structure is useless or that learned attention identifies intent.
